items.title: Canadian regulators tighten prediction market rules, barring leverage and sports contracts in the dealer model, Bonus reports
items.content_text: - **Canadian regulators tighten prediction market rules, barring leverage and sports contracts in the dealer model, Bonus reports** — Bonus reported Canadian Securities Administrators and CIRO staff published a joint notice on August 27, 2026 saying dealer-members may not allow clients to use leverage or margin on event contracts, and permitted contracts must have an initial term to maturity of 30 days or longer. The notice said sports and entertainment contracts should not be regulated within securities and derivatives legislation, CIRO staff said facilitating them was not appropriate for dealer-members, and contracts tied to elections or political events are not permitted within the dealer model. ([Bonus](https://www.bonus.com/ca/news/canadian-prediction-market-rules-2026/))

items.title: Portugal gambling regulator SRIJ orders Polymarket to halt operations after more than 4 million euros wagered on presidential election before results, GambleRss reports
items.content_text: - **Portugal gambling regulator SRIJ orders Polymarket to halt operations after more than 4 million euros wagered on presidential election before results, GambleRss reports** — GambleRss, reporting a Casino.org story published October 24, said Portugal's gambling regulator SRIJ confirmed it ordered Polymarket to halt operations because the platform is illegal under national rules that limit online gambling to licensed sports betting, casino games and horse racing, not political event markets. ([GambleRss](https://gamblerss.com/portugal-blocks-polymarket-after-e4m-election-betting-surge-54744))

items.title: Polymarket paid creators to stage up to 1.9 million dollars in fake winning bets on a copycat site, WSJ investigation reported by BitRss finds
items.content_text: - **Polymarket paid creators to stage up to 1.9 million dollars in fake winning bets on a copycat site, WSJ investigation reported by BitRss finds** — BitRss, reporting a Wall Street Journal investigation published October 24, said Polymarket paid college-age creators 2,000 to 3,000 dollars a month to post videos of bets seemingly won on its platform, while the trades were actually placed on dummy sites such as poiymarket.com and had no blockchain trace. items.content_text: - **Tiger Research finds prediction market prices serve as data for media, ICE and the Federal Reserve, HTX reports** — Tiger Research argues the core value of prediction markets is producing probability data, noting Google Finance, CNBC, CNN and the Wall Street Journal now display market probabilities while ICE and Tradeweb distribute the data to institutional clients. The study analyzed 556 active and 2,681 settled markets on Limitless and cites a Federal Reserve working paper that treats prediction market data as a macro expectations benchmark.
